issue.title: [PRD-03] Organizations and Organization Membership
issue.body:
## Implementation ticket

This ticket implements **PRD-03** from the approved StrataAI product requirements.

### Adopted StrataAI2 architecture
Implementation must use the adopted StrataAI2 architecture:
- React + TypeScript + Vite + **MUI/Material UI**; MUI is the primary component/styling system.
- `dnd-kit` (or approved equivalent) for accessible Kanban drag/drop.
- ASP.NET Core modular monolith with physical `Domain`, `Application`, `Infrastructure`, `Api`, and `Worker` project boundaries.
- PostgreSQL as the primary datastore, RLS for defence-in-depth tenant isolation, and pgvector for semantic retrieval where required.
- Object storage for binary files.
- Separate API and Worker processes from the same codebase.
- PostgreSQL-backed durable jobs/transactional outbox initially; do not introduce RabbitMQ/Kafka/Redis without an ADR.
- SignalR for realtime browser collaboration where required.
- Docker images for web, API, and Worker built once, tested, and emitted by CI.

# PRD-03 — Organizations and Organization Membership

## 1. PRD Identifier
**PRD-03**

## 2. Feature Name
**Organizations and Organization Membership**

## 3. Executive Summary
Defines organization creation, editing, membership, roles, invitations, board directory, leave/delete behavior, and organization-level governance.

## 4. Problem Statement
A Trello-class collaborative Kanban product appears simple at the surface but depends on precise domain rules, authorization, lifecycle semantics, concurrency controls, and predictable interaction behavior. This PRD defines the behavior required for **Organizations and Organization Membership** without relying on proprietary implementation details.

## 5. Product Objective
Deliver a testable, production-oriented implementation of this domain that integrates consistently with the canonical Organization → Board → List → Card model.

## 6. User Personas
- **Organization Owner/Admin** — governs membership and organization-level configuration.
- **Board Admin** — manages board-level collaboration and controls.
- **Contributor** — creates and changes work items.
- **Viewer** — inspects content without mutation rights.
- **Public Visitor** — may inspect PUBLIC boards only where permitted.

## 7. User Stories
- As a user, I can create a organization.
- As a user, I can invite and remove members.
- As a user, I can see all boards in a organization.
- As a user, I can leave or delete a organization when authorized.

## 8. Functional Requirements
- **WS-FR-001** — Authenticated users SHALL be able to create a organization.
- **WS-FR-002** — Organization fields SHALL include name, description, logo/avatar, owner, status, createdAt, updatedAt.
- **WS-FR-003** — Organization admins SHALL be able to rename and edit organization metadata.
- **WS-FR-004** — Authorized users SHALL be able to invite members by email.
- **WS-FR-005** — Organization admins SHALL be able to remove members subject to ownership safeguards.
- **WS-FR-006** — Members SHALL be able to leave a organization unless they are the sole owner/admin required for continuity.
- **WS-FR-007** — The organization home SHALL list all boards the current user is authorized to discover.
- **WS-FR-008** — Organization roles SHALL include OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER.
- **WS-FR-009** — Deleting a organization SHALL require explicit confirmation and SHALL be restricted to authorized owners.
- **WS-FR-010** — Organization deletion SHALL define treatment of boards, lists, cards, attachments, and audit records.

## 9. Detailed Interaction Behaviour
- Changes should appear immediately using optimistic updates when rollback/reconciliation is safe.
- The server is authoritative for authorization, validation, version, and persisted state.
- Shared-state changes emit domain events and become visible to other authorized clients through the realtime layer.
- Destructive operations follow PRD-18 lifecycle rules.
- Controls unavailable to the user may be hidden/disabled for UX, but the same action must still be rejected server-side.

## 10. Business Rules
- Every board belongs to one organization.
- A organization must retain at least one owner until deletion.
- Invitation acceptance may require authentication or registration.

## 11. Permission Rules
- `VIEW`: depends on board/organization visibility and membership.
- `CREATE`: requires authenticated membership and the relevant create permission.
- `EDIT`: requires edit rights to the entity's board.
- `MOVE`: requires edit/move rights in both source and destination contexts where applicable.
- `COMMENT`: requires authenticated board participation unless future policy explicitly allows otherwise.
- `INVITE`: requires board/organization administrative rights.
- `ARCHIVE` / `RESTORE`: require edit or administrative rights according to entity policy.
- `DELETE`: requires elevated permission and lifecycle preconditions.
- `ADMINISTER`: limited to the relevant admin/owner role.
- Every permission is enforced on the server; UI state is never the security boundary.

## 12. Data Requirements
Organization, OrganizationMember, Invitation. Unique membership on (organizationId,userId). Invitation tokens unique and expiring.

All mutable records require `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. Concurrency-sensitive records require a version/revision field. Foreign-key or equivalent integrity checks must prevent cross-board/cross-organization inconsistencies.

## 13. API Requirements
POST /organizations; PATCH /organizations/{id}; DELETE /organizations/{id}; GET /organizations/{id}/boards; POST /organizations/{id}/invitations; DELETE /organizations/{id}/members/{userId}

General API rules:
- Schema-validate all input.
- Return consistent error envelopes.
- Enforce authorization before protected disclosure.
- Support idempotency for retry-prone mutations.
- Use cursor pagination for unbounded collections.
- Return updated entity version after successful concurrency-sensitive mutations.

## 14. Real-Time / Event Requirements
The following events are directly relevant:
- `ORGANIZATION_CREATED`
- `ORGANIZATION_UPDATED`
- `ORGANIZATION_MEMBER_INVITED`
- `ORGANIZATION_MEMBER_ADDED`
- `ORGANIZATION_MEMBER_REMOVED`
- `ORGANIZATION_DELETED`

Events must contain `eventId`, `eventType`, `actorId`, `organizationId`, `boardId`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `version` where relevant, `metadata`, and `createdAt`. Clients deduplicate by `eventId`.

## 15. UX Requirements
- Primary desktop interactions must remain fast and visually direct.
- All critical actions remain available on tablet and mobile web.
- Destructive actions require explicit confirmation.
- Empty/loading/error states must not shift the user into ambiguous contexts.
- The UI should preserve board scroll/list context when opening and closing card detail.

## 16. Accessibility Requirements
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
- All interactive controls require accessible names.
- Visible keyboard focus is mandatory.
- Pointer drag/drop has keyboard equivalent where movement is involved.
- Dialogs manage focus correctly.
- Color is never the sole status indicator.
- Realtime changes that affect the current operation use non-disruptive accessible announcements.

## 17. Error and Empty States
- Empty state: explain the next permitted action.
- Permission denied: state that access/action is unavailable without leaking protected metadata.
- Validation error: identify the affected field/action.
- Network timeout: preserve recoverable client state and offer retry.
- Conflict: reconcile to server state and explain that the item changed elsewhere.
- Deleted/missing entity: distinguish not-found from inaccessible only where doing so is safe.

## 18. Edge Cases
- Concurrent edits from multiple authorized clients.
- User loses permission while the entity is open.
- Parent board/list becomes archived during editing.
- Duplicate client submission after timeout.
- Realtime event arrives before mutation response.
- Realtime event is missed during disconnect and recovered later.
- Entity is moved while another user is viewing its detail.
- Very large boards requiring virtualization.

## 19. Non-Functional Requirements
- Board initial usable rendering target: **<1.5 s** under documented normal conditions.
- Simple movement visual feedback target: **<100 ms**.
- Server mutation acknowledgement target: **p95 <500 ms**.
- Cached card-detail opening target: **<200 ms**.
- Design supports at least **200 lists/board**, **5,000 cards/board**, and **100,000 archived cards/organization**.
- Log errors with correlation IDs but avoid logging sensitive content bodies by default.

## 20. Analytics / Telemetry
Track:
- feature open/use counts;
- mutation latency and success/failure;
- permission denials by stable error code;
- realtime reconnect/conflict rates;
- client exceptions;
- user-visible retry events.
Do not use analytics events as the source of truth for audit history.

## 21. Dependencies
- PRD-02
- PRD-05
- PRD-18

## 22. Out of Scope
Cross-organization administration, billing, public template marketplace.

## 23. Acceptance Criteria
**AC-WS-03-01**
GIVEN an authorized user is using this feature
WHEN the user performs the primary supported action associated with WS-FR-001
THEN the server validates authorization and input
AND the resulting state is persisted
AND the client reflects the authoritative result.

**AC-WS-03-02**
GIVEN the same operation would violate the rule represented by WS-FR-003
WHEN the user or client attempts the operation
THEN the server rejects it with a stable error code
AND protected state is unchanged
AND no unauthorized information is disclosed.

**AC-WS-03-03**
GIVEN two clients have the same board or entity open
WHEN a successful mutation relevant to WS-FR-010 occurs
THEN the initiating client receives confirmation
AND other authorized clients receive or recover the updated state without requiring a full manual reload.

## 24. Test Scenarios
1. Primary happy path.
2. Empty-state behavior.
3. Invalid input.
4. Unauthorized user.
5. User loses permission mid-session.
6. Network timeout and retry.
7. Duplicate request/idempotency.
8. Two-client concurrent update.
9. Realtime disconnect/reconnect recovery.
10. Archived/deleted parent behavior.
11. Keyboard-only operation.
12. Mobile viewport.
13. Large-data performance case where applicable.

## 25. Definition of Done
- All functional requirements implemented.
- Server-side authorization tests pass.
- Schema and migration changes reviewed.
- Domain events emitted and consumed where required.
- Unit, integration, and end-to-end tests pass.
- Accessibility checks and keyboard scenarios pass.
- Error/empty/loading states are implemented.
- Telemetry is documented.
- No known P0/P1 defects.
- Product behavior is documented sufficiently that another team does not need to invent missing core rules.

## 26. Open Questions
- Any unresolved implementation choice discovered during development must be recorded explicitly.
- If a choice changes cross-PRD behavior, the affected PRDs and traceability mappings must be updated before release.

---

## Linked test cases

These test IDs are part of this GitHub ticket. Implementation tests should reference the corresponding PRD/AC/test ID in the test name, metadata, source comment, or traceability manifest.

- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-01** — Primary happy path.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-02** — Empty-state behavior.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-03** — Invalid input.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-04** — Unauthorized user.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-05** — User loses permission mid-session.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-06** — Network timeout and retry.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-07** — Duplicate request/idempotency.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-08** — Two-client concurrent update.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-09** — Realtime disconnect/reconnect recovery.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-10** — Archived/deleted parent behavior.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-11** — Keyboard-only operation.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-12** — Mobile viewport.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-13** — Large-data performance case where applicable.

## Agent execution contract
- Implement the PRD requirements and acceptance criteria; do not silently narrow scope.
- Preserve Organization/tenant isolation and the separate Owner Portal authorization surface.
- Add/update automated tests before closing the ticket.
- Include required schema migrations, authorization checks, events, audit behaviour, accessibility, errors, empty states, concurrency and observability.
- Link the implementation pull request to this issue and include executed test evidence in the PR description.
- If a material PRD/architecture conflict is discovered, stop that conflicting design decision and document it rather than inventing behaviour.


## Strata Work UX acceptance (2026-10-17)

Additive requirements for the touched UI slices; existing FR/AC/test IDs, permissions, audit/lifecycle rules and parent completion conditions remain. This adds no dependency on the entire redesign and changes no approval or voting authority.

**User problem, role and outcome:** 01, 03, 04: participant cannot locate daily work among unrelated entities; find authorized boards

**Entry, workflow, visible fields and hierarchy:** Context top bar → Work → board directory → board. Persistent desktop navigation; phone menu. Account/search separate; owner/admin administration separate in the current OrganizationHome disclosure, using its admitted summary. Page title and primary create action precede secondary operations.

**Permissions, privacy, state/recovery, dependencies, exclusions and migration:** Surface admission before disclosure; owner/admin controls from current server role; denial clears context. Loading has no stale role disclosure, retry on failure. Existing routes retained; no schema migration. No pretend dashboard or disabled feature links. Shared loading/empty/error/success, keyboard/focus, responsive and safe-retry requirements in [the work contract](https://github.com/nickmailhot-lang/StrataAI2/blob/ux/strata-workflows-20261017/docs/ux/prd-amendments.md) also apply. Existing server authorization remains decisive.

**Observable acceptance and validation:** UX-NAV-01: Work has aria-current on directory and all board descendants. UX-NAV-02: phone menu opens/closes by keyboard and restores focus. UX-NAV-03: OrganizationHome exposes only role-permitted actions from its currently admitted summary, including synchronous withdrawal. Unit + desktop/phone browser navigation and denial tests.

**Traceability and completion evidence:** [design-rule and slice mapping](https://github.com/nickmailhot-lang/StrataAI2/blob/ux/strata-workflows-20261017/docs/ux/prd-amendments.md), [current repository audit](https://github.com/nickmailhot-lang/StrataAI2/blob/ux/strata-workflows-20261017/docs/ux/current-state.md), [single delivery ledger](https://github.com/nickmailhot-lang/StrataAI2/blob/ux/strata-workflows-20261017/docs/ux/delivery-report.md). [Draft implementation PR #100](https://github.com/nickmailhot-lang/StrataAI2/pull/100) provides reviewable increments; implemented, tested and accepted are separate. Planned criteria remain open. Documentation/source tests alone do not close this PRD.
